T2M.name: Air temperature
T2M.definition: How warm the air is about 2 meters above the ground.

TQV.name: Water vapor in the air
TQV.definition: All the water vapor in a column of air, written as how deep it would be if it all fell as liquid water.

PRECTOTCORR.name: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.definition: Rain and snow reaching the ground (bias-corrected with rain gauge data).

EVAP.name: Evaporation
EVAP.definition: Water moving from the surface (land, plants, ocean) up into the air.

GWETROOT.name: Root-zone soil moisture
GWETROOT.definition: How wet the soil is down where plant roots reach (0% = bone dry, 100% = fully soaked). Land only.

SNOMAS.name: Snow amount
SNOMAS.definition: How much snow is sitting on the ground, measured by weight per square meter. Land only.

RUNOFF.name: Surface runoff
RUNOFF.definition: Water that flows over the land surface into streams and rivers instead of soaking in. Land only.

TOTEXTTAU.name: Haze / aerosols
TOTEXTTAU.definition: How much sunlight is blocked by tiny particles in the air like smoke, dust, and pollution. Higher = hazier.
TOTEXTTAU.caveat: MERRA-2 aerosol trends can partly come from changes in which satellites were fed into the model over time (AVHRR, then MODIS and MISR), not only from the real air.

DUEXTTAU.name: Dust in the air
DUEXTTAU.definition: The part of the haze that comes from desert dust.
DUEXTTAU.caveat: MERRA-2 aerosol trends can partly come from changes in which satellites were fed into the model over time (AVHRR, then MODIS and MISR), not only from the real air.

regions.name: Whole Earth
regions.blurb: The planet as a whole. A baseline for comparing everything else.

regions.name: Arctic
regions.blurb: Everything north of the Arctic Circle: sea ice, tundra, and Greenland's north.

regions.name: Greenland
regions.blurb: The world's largest island, mostly covered by a thick ice sheet.

regions.name: Siberian forests
regions.blurb: Vast cold forests (taiga) sitting on frozen ground (permafrost).

regions.name: Sahara Desert
regions.blurb: The largest hot desert on Earth and the biggest source of airborne dust.

regions.name: Sahel
regions.blurb: The dry grassland belt south of the Sahara that depends on a short rainy season.

regions.name: Arabian Peninsula
regions.blurb: Hot, dry desert with frequent dust storms.

regions.name: Amazon rainforest
regions.blurb: The largest tropical rainforest, which recycles its own rain through evaporation.

regions.name: Congo rainforest
regions.blurb: Africa's great rainforest, the second largest on Earth.

regions.name: US Southwest
regions.blurb: Arizona, New Mexico, Nevada and southern California, home to the Colorado River.

regions.name: US Corn Belt
regions.blurb: Some of the most productive farmland in the world.

regions.name: New Jersey
regions.blurb: A coastal state between two big estuaries: Delaware Bay and New York Harbor.

regions.name: Chesapeake Bay
regions.blurb: The largest estuary in the US, where rivers mix with the ocean tide.

regions.name: Mediterranean
regions.blurb: Southern Europe and the sea around it. Hot, dry summers and wet winters.

regions.name: European Alps
regions.blurb: Europe's highest mountains, where snow and glaciers feed major rivers.

regions.name: Himalaya & Tibet
regions.blurb: The 'third pole': high mountains whose snow feeds rivers for over a billion people.

regions.name: Delhi & Ganges Plain
regions.blurb: One of the most densely populated regions on Earth, known for heavy air pollution.

regions.name: Beijing region
regions.blurb: China's capital and its surrounding industrial region.

regions.name: Los Angeles basin
regions.blurb: A huge city in a basin surrounded by mountains that trap smog.

regions.name: Murray-Darling Basin
regions.blurb: Australia's main farming river basin, hit hard by long droughts.

regions.name: Central Pacific (El Niño zone)
regions.blurb: The patch of ocean where El Niño and La Niña are measured.

sanity.reference: Rantanen et al. 2022 (observations, 1979-2021): Arctic 0.73 vs global 0.19 °C/decade, ratio about 3.8
sanity.note: Reanalyses disagree on Arctic trends (roughly 0.3 to 0.7 °C/decade over 1980-2013), so a MERRA-2 ratio a little below the observed one is expected.

sources.data: NASA GMAO MERRA-2 monthly reanalysis (M2TMNXSLV, M2TMNXFLX, M2TMNXLND, M2TMNXAER v5.12.4), via NASA GES DISC
